Blood lactate accumulation depends on both how much lactate is being produced and released into the bloodstream, and how quickly it is being removed from the blood.  
Option (A) only considers muscle lactate production and efflux, but lactate can also be produced elsewhere and cleared by other organs.  
Option (B) focuses only on production from anaerobic glycolysis, ignoring clearance.  
Option (C) is unrelated because glucose uptake does not directly determine lactate accumulation.  
Option (D) correctly captures the balance between lactate appearance (from all sources) and lactate clearance (by liver, kidneys, etc.), which determines the net accumulation in blood.  

Final answer: (D)
